passages.text: OVERVIEW AT&T Inc. is referred to as “we,” “AT&T” or the “Company” throughout this document. AT&T products and services are provided or offered by subsidiaries and affiliates of AT&T Inc. under the AT&T brand and not by AT&T Inc., and the names of the particular subsidiaries and affiliates providing the services generally have been omitted. AT&T is a holding company whose subsidiaries and affiliates operate worldwide in the telecommunications and technology industries. You should read this discussion in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes (Notes). Our Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations included in this document generally discusses 2025 and 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussions of 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this document can be found in “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10 ‑ K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024. We have two reportable segments: Communications and Latin America. Our segment results presented in Note 4 and discussed below follow our internal management reporting. Each segment’s percentage calculation of total segment operating revenue is derived from our segment results table in Note 4. Segment operating income is primarily attributable to our Communications segment due to prior-years operating losses in Latin America. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: In addition to the other information set forth in this document, including the matters contained under the heading “Cautionary Language Concerning Forward-Looking Statements,” you should carefully read the matters described below. We believe that each of these matters could materially affect our business. Most, if not all, of these factors are beyond our ability to control. Macro-Economic Factors: Adverse changes in the U.S. securities markets, a higher interest rate environment, rising inflation and medical costs could materially increase our benefit plan costs and future funding requirements. Our costs to provide current benefits and funding for future benefits are subject to increases, primarily due to continuing increases in medical and prescription drug costs, in part due to inflation, and can be affected by lower returns on assets held by our pension and other benefit plans, which are reflected in our financial statements for that year. In calculating the recognized benefit costs, we have made certain assumptions regarding future investment returns, interest rates and medical costs. These assumptions could change significantly over time and could be materially different than originally projected. Lower than assumed investment returns, an increase in our benefit obligations, and higher than assumed medical and prescription drug costs will increase expenses. The Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) requires companies to recognize the funded status of defined benefit pension and postretirement plans as an asset or liability in their statement of financial position and to recognize changes in that funded status in the year in which the changes occur. We have elected to reflect the annual adjustments to the funded status in our consolidated statement of income. Therefore, an increase in our costs or adverse market conditions will have a negative effect on our operating results. Significant adverse changes in capital markets could result in the deterioration of our defined benefit plans’ funded status. Inflationary pressures on costs, such as inputs for devices we sell and network components, labor and distribution costs, may impact our network construction, our financial condition or results of operations. As a provider of telecommunications and technology services, we sell handsets, wireless data cards, wireless computing devices and customer premises equipment manufactured by various suppliers for use with our voice and data services and depend on suppliers to provide us, directly or through other suppliers, with items such as network equipment, customer premises equipment, and wireless-related equipment such as mobile hotspots, handsets, wirelessly enabled computers, wireless data cards and other connected devices for our customers. In recent years, the costs of these inputs and the costs of labor necessary to develop, deploy and maintain our networks and our products and services have increased. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital spending plus shareholder distributions, leaving a modest surplus for debt reduction; the cushion is thinner than at higher-rated peers, so sustained capital intensity would erode it.

Operating margin improved year over year and now matches the sector median, reflecting Communications segment scale and cost discipline; margin parity supports stable EBITDA generation through the wireless and fiber investment cycle.

key_risks.text: Gross leverage sits above the sector median and net leverage is roughly double the peer median, placing the issuer in the intermediate risk band with limited headroom to the next boundary; a modest EBITDA decline would push leverage into a weaker tier.

The debt note shows a large concentration of notes maturing after year five, with meaningful near-term maturities and a rising current-maturity balance; refinancing this book at prevailing rates keeps interest expense elevated and constrains deleveraging.

Risk factors flag inflation in network equipment, devices and labor plus pension and benefit funding sensitivity to capital markets; these cost pressures could compress the operating margin that currently anchors coverage.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage improved year over year but remains below the sector median, and EBITDA coverage is likewise weaker than peers; cash flow to debt also trails the median, indicating comparatively thinner debt-service cushion.

Free cash flow covers dividends and buybacks with a modest margin, and cash flow to net debt sits above the downgrade threshold; distributions absorb a large share of internally generated funds, limiting discretionary deleveraging.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer is a scaled telecommunications operator with stable revenue and improving operating income, but leverage above the sector median and coverage below peers place it in the intermediate risk band; the indicative profile is not a rating.

Our judgement is a stable but constrained credit trajectory: cash generation funds capital spending and distributions, yet the current ratio below one and peer-relative leverage leave little room for adverse cost or rate shocks without accelerated debt paydown.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流充裕覆蓋資本開支加股東分派，留有溫和盈餘用於減債；緩衝較評級較高同業為薄，若資本密集程度持續將侵蝕該緩衝。
營運利潤率按年改善，現已與行業中位數看齊，反映通訊業務分部的規模與成本紀律；利潤率持平有助於在無線及光纖投資週期中維持穩定的 EBITDA 產生。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿高於行業中位數，淨槓桿約為同業中位數的兩倍，使發行人處於中等風險區間，距下一界限的空間有限；EBITDA 溫和下降將把槓桿推入較弱層級。
債務附註顯示大量票據於第五年後到期，同時存在可觀的近期到期債務及上升的流動到期餘額；按現行利率為此債務組合再融資將使利息支出維持高企，並制約去槓桿。
風險因素指出網絡設備、終端設備及勞動力通脹，加上退休金及福利供款對資本市場的敏感度；這些成本壓力可能壓縮目前支撐覆蓋率的營運利潤率。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率按年改善但仍低於行業中位數，EBITDA 覆蓋率同樣弱於同業；現金流對債務比率亦落後於中位數，顯示償債緩衝相對較薄。
自由現金流以溫和幅度覆蓋股息及回購，現金流對淨債務比率高於降級門檻；分派佔內部產生資金的比例較大，限制自主去槓桿空間。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人為具規模的電訊營運商，收入穩定且營運收入改善，但槓桿高於行業中位數且覆蓋率低於同業，使其處於中等風險區間；指示性概況並非評級。
我們的判斷為穩定但受限的信用軌跡：現金產生足以支持資本開支及分派，然而流動比率低於一及相對同業的槓桿水平，令其在成本或利率不利衝擊下幾無空間，除非加快償債。
